text:
In the court of an old king lived a man called the Fool. He wore bright clothes and made everybody laugh, but he was cleverer than the ministers.

One day, the king gave him a golden staff and said, “Keep this until you find someone who is a bigger fool than you. Then give it to him.”

Years passed. The Fool carried the staff everywhere. Eventually, the king fell gravely ill. The Fool visited him and found him very weak.

“I am going on a long journey,” said the king in a faint voice.

“When will you return?” asked the Fool.

“I will never return.”

“Have you prepared for it? Have you sent servants ahead? Have you packed your possessions?”

“No,” whispered the king. “Nothing can be taken with me. I will go alone.”

The Fool stood up and placed the golden staff in the king’s hands. “Then this belongs to you,” he said. “I have met many people who worried about small things, but you are the greatest fool of all. You spent your whole life collecting treasures, and you never thought about the one journey that really matters.”

The king looked at the staff and began to weep, but his tears were not of anger. In his final days, he gave away much of his wealth and made peace with his enemies.

Moral: Don’t spend your whole life preparing for everything except what truly matters.

quiz.q: The king gave the Fool a golden staff.
The king had prepared well for his long journey.
What journey was the king talking about?
What did the king do in his final days?
o: Gave away much of his wealth and made peace
